outcome.answer: Yes—several of the papers use graph-based machine learning for chemical reactions. RxnCLF builds on a condensed reaction graph to learn transformation-aware representations and improves reaction yield prediction, outperforming graph and sequence baselines [1]. enviGraph uses a graph-to-sequence predictor for biodegradation pathway prediction, pretraining on synthetic reaction data [6]. More broadly, one paper on chemical property prediction shows how graph neural networks can be improved with layer-to-layer knowledge mixing, but it is not specifically about reactions [9].
